author: Stimulating
body:
DISCLAIMER: This is not a staff bashfest and is made with good intentions, this is something that I realized may be the real issue, that hasn't been brought up. No, I do not intend to flame, or get into any flame wars, and I'm not going to fight about something as negligible as people getting mad about my opinion at this point.

Ok, so recently (almost a week ago now) I made a forum post based around trying to help out staff (https://avicus.net/forums/3754a273f), being as open as I could, affirming I wouldn't trashtalk you or speak poorly of you if you came to me, because it was admirable that you wanted to improve and actually try, and giving you options to contact me privately. 

In the end only one staff member out of the entire team asked me for help, even after making myself as approachable as possible, so it's either the staff team doesn't think they need help at all with their hack/autoclicker detection, or the staff team just Isn't enthusiastic enough. 
It's not like I'm going to throw you under because you did something that I respect (which I made clear in the post). 

This is not supposed to be a slamfest, but it seems like I gave the staff a good opportunity to improve, only one took the opportunity, and I'm not going to run to you to save you or help you. If you want help, if you truly want to improve, and if you cared...why wouldn't you take any opportunity you got? 

I didn't know if this person wanted to be named or not, so I left their IGN out. I hope this is a wake-up call... 

I'll still accept if anyone wants help, I'll be glad to, because that's respectable. I will not make a list, because I know some staff are good enough that they may not need as much help (like iz and Aex/TNT). I will not shame you in public if you haven't asked me for help either. 

Edit: 2 staff members now

replies.author: Stimulating
replies.body:
Just because I'm not part of the staff team does not mean I don't have lots of experience with hacks. They can benefit because I know the hacks very well, and know a bunch a little things that really help to detect them, that are often overlooked.

Ex: triggerbotters have hit registration beyond that of what their ms should allow, and will often hit you while they are being kb'd backwards away from you. Headtwitches are mainly caused by the fact that triggerbot hits the other person as soon as their crosshair enters the body, so if the person just drags their crosshair across their hitbox for a split second, they get hit, which wouldn't normally happen, which creates the appearance of them hitting you out of your hitbox. I have more info as well, and videos to reference off.
